variants.usage_rule: Use at least 3 different button variants per page. Never use the same style for primary and secondary CTAs.
variants.disposition: Sharp (rounded-none or rounded-sm) is the DEFAULT button shape. It signals design confidence. Pill (rounded-full) is the safe, uncommitted choice — use it ONLY if the reference sites specifically use pill buttons and you can articulate why. Default to sharp.

variants.anti_slop_note: Bento grids MUST have mixed tile sizes (use 2x1, 1x2, 2x2 spans). Never make all tiles the same size with the same rounded-xl border and gradient. Vary radii, spans, and background treatments across tiles.

variants.failure_modes: HIGH RISK PRIMITIVE. Fails badly with: generic stock images (looks like dark void), low-opacity inactive text (looks broken), scroll height >300vh (scroll desert). ONLY use if you have 4+ distinct, high-contrast product screenshots that will be clearly visible. If using generic Unsplash images, DO NOT use this primitive — use a simpler tabbed layout or stepped cards instead.

Needs 6-8 cards MINIMUM to justify scroll hijacking. 4 cards with gaps = empty. Cards should be wide (500px+) and visually rich, not narrow text cards. Scroll height should be 150-200vh max, not 300-500vh.

variants.anti_slop_note: VARY your border-radius across cards. Never use the same radius on every card. Mix sharp (rounded-none) with subtle (rounded-lg) — uniform rounded-2xl everywhere is a banned pattern.

The aurora effect is achieved with CSS keyframes animating background-position on a multi-stop gradient, not with absolutely-positioned blurred divs. If you find yourself writing blur(80px) on a colored div, you are doing it wrong — that is the banned floating-orbs pattern.

variants.implementation_recipe: Layer 1: CSS gradient (linear/radial/conic) on a div. Layer 2: SVG feTurbulence noise at 4-8% opacity via ::after pseudo-element. Layer 3: Optional CSS filter on the gradient container (contrast+saturate for punch, or blur for soft mesh). Result: rich, non-generic gradient that looks textured and photographically real — not flat CSS. The grain breaks up banding artifacts and the filter adjustment adds depth that raw gradients lack.
variants.usage_rule: NEVER use a raw CSS gradient without a texture layer. Unfiltered gradients look like 2018 landing page slop. Always add at minimum a grain/noise overlay. For maximum impact: gradient + grain + contrast boost + subtle blur on edges.
variants.anti_slop_note: This is a SINGLE gradient element with filter treatments applied to it. NOT multiple colored divs with blur. The gradient is a CSS gradient (linear/radial/conic) on ONE container, with noise/grain overlaid via a ::after pseudo-element. Never create multiple blurred blobs.

variants.implementation_note: backdrop-filter: blur() is the key CSS property. Combine with semi-transparent background-color (bg-white/60 or bg-black/20) and a subtle border (border-white/20) for edge definition. Works on any element placed over colored/image content. The blur creates depth separation that shadows alone cannot achieve.

blend_modes: multiply — darkens, great for text over light images
color — applies hue+saturation of element to underlying content
luminosity — preserves brightness of element over underlying color
applications: text-with-mix-blend-difference-over-image — text inverts based on image brightness

combinations: inner-glow + border-white/10 + backdrop-blur = glass with edge
variants.implementation: box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.1), inset 0 0 20px rgba(255,255,255,0.05); This creates a subtle light-catch on the top edge and a soft interior glow. Combined with a dark background and a 1px border at 10% white, it creates a glass-like surface that feels 3D without any 3D rendering.

application_rules: ONLY on 1-2 words maximum per page — never full headings
ONLY on display-weight text (font-bold or font-black)
ONLY with high-contrast gradient stops (not muddy transitions)
NEVER on body text or navigation
color_strategies: warm-to-cool-shift — eg amber to teal for energy feel
variants.anti_slop_note: Gradient text is BANNED as a default heading treatment (see banned_patterns). This primitive exists ONLY for selective, intentional accent use — one emphasized word in a heading, a brand statement, or a key metric. If more than 2 words have gradient text on the entire page, you are overusing it.

variants.anti_template_note: The default instinct is to keep everything in its grid cell, cleanly separated. Award-winning sites BREAK the grid — images bleed into adjacent sections, text overlaps image boundaries, cards fan out from a stack. This primitive forces intentional overlap that creates editorial depth and visual hierarchy.

techniques: background-color-interpolation-via-useTransform — bg shifts from white to dark as you scroll
text-color-shift-at-section-boundaries — text adapts to section bg

variants.implementation: Use useScroll to get scrollYProgress (0-1 for full page), then useTransform to map progress ranges to color values. Apply to a wrapper div's backgroundColor. For section-specific shifts, use the section ref with useScroll({target: ref}). Interpolate between oklch values for perceptually smooth color transitions.

techniques: background-highlight-mark — colored bg behind key words (like a highlighter pen)
weight-contrast-split — light weight + bold weight in same headline
color-accent-word — one word in brand color, rest in neutral
italic-accent — key word in serif italic within sans-serif heading
underline-accent — thick decorative underline on emphasis word (not text-underline, a real element)
size-contrast — one word at 1.2x size of surrounding text
variants.implementation_note: Wrap the emphasis word in a <span> with distinct styling. For highlight: use inline-block with a background-color and slight padding. For weight contrast: use font-thin on most words and font-black on emphasis. The key is SELECTIVE application — 1 word per heading maximum. This breaks typographic monotony without resorting to gradient text.

gradient-hero → white → slate-50 → dark-with-image → white → gradient-cta

section_treatments: plain-white — MAXIMUM 2 per page, never adjacent
off-white-slate-50 — neutral divider, no more than 2 adjacent
dark-slate-900 — high contrast, must use at least once per page
image-background — full-bleed with dark overlay for text
variants.enforcement_rule: NO TWO ADJACENT SECTIONS may have the same background treatment. Maximum 2 plain-white sections per page. Every page MUST include at least one dark section, one gradient or textured section, and one section with a real image background. This primitive is the single most effective way to prevent template-grade output — it forces visual variety by construction.

— Color arrays should shift hue gradually: pick 12 oklch values going from cool (hue 240) to warm (hue 40), each step about 15-20 hue degrees apart. The strips create a rich, sophisticated gradient effect that looks designed, not generated. See delve.co hero for the canonical example.
patterns: vertical-strips — 10-16 equal-width columns, each a different color
variable-width-strips — some strips wider for visual rhythm
with-content-overlay — text/cards floated over the strip grid via absolute positioning
partial-coverage — strips cover part of the section, rest is solid color
variants.usage_rule: This is the PREFERRED gradient treatment for hero and CTA sections. Do NOT use CSS linear-gradient for backgrounds. Stepped panels look sophisticated and designed. Continuous gradients look AI-generated.
variants.palette_guidance: WARM palettes (amber, gold, orange): use as PARTIAL coverage only (bottom 30% of section, or one side of a split). Never as full-section background — it flattens hierarchy and makes text hard to read. COOL palettes (blue, teal, navy): safe for full-section backgrounds. MIXED cool-to-warm: the most sophisticated — start cool on the left, shift to warm on the right. Creates visual movement. NEVER use your accent color as the dominant background color — it overwhelms. Each page must use a DIFFERENT palette for its stepped gradient.

motion_primitives.description: Section enters with upward offset and staggered children. Use staggerChildren: 0.08s.
Horizontal slide in for split layouts. Left panel slides from left, right panel from right.
Element enters with blur(8px) + scale(0.96) → clear + scale(1). Premium feel.
Minor scale + opacity change for cards and buttons. scale: 1.02, quick.
Element drifts up to 8px toward cursor on hover using onMouseMove + framer-motion animate. Best for CTAs and nav items.
Subtle y-transform tied to scroll progress via useScroll+useTransform. Range: [0, 200px] → [-30px, 30px].
Image moves at 60% of scroll speed creating depth. useScroll on section → useTransform translateY. Makes layouts feel multi-layered.
Text slides up from behind a clip-path mask. Container: overflow-hidden. Child: translateY(100%) → 0. Elegant line-by-line reveal.
Number counts up from 0 to final value when viewport enters. Use useMotionValue + animate. Great for stats sections.
Grid items enter diagonally — stagger by column index + row index combined. Creates a wave-like cascade across a grid.
SVG feTurbulence noise layer at 4–8% opacity over images. Apply via ::after pseudo-element. Adds analog film texture with zero JS.
When Vaul drawer opens, scale the background content to 96% with border-radius 12px. Creates iOS-native depth illusion.
canvas-confetti burst of 100 particles from bottom-center on form success, purchase complete, or achievement unlock.
Skeleton shimmer placeholders cross-fade to real content with blur(4px) → blur(0) + opacity 0 → 1 transition.

Background color morphs between values as user scrolls. Use useScroll({target: wrapperRef}) + useTransform to interpolate between oklch colors. Apply to a wrapper div. Creates immersive narrative scroll.
Each child element enters with blur(12px) + translateY(20px) → clear + translateY(0), staggered by 0.06s. More premium than simple fade-up. Use filter property in framer-motion variants.

Card tilts toward cursor in 3D space on hover. Calculate rotateX/rotateY from cursor position relative to card center. Use perspective(800px) on parent, transform on card. Max rotation: 8deg. Very premium feel.

better_alternatives: horizontal-scroll-panels — each step occupies a full viewport-width panel that scrolls left-to-right
visual-pipeline — goods/data physically moves across screen with animated connectors between stages
overlapping-reveal-cards — each step card overlaps the previous one as you scroll, creating depth
split-screen-progression — screen splits 50/50, each side tells a parallel story (before/after)
full-bleed-stage-sections — each step is its own full-viewport section with unique visual treatment
product_walkthrough.composition_recipe: Make each step feel like a DIFFERENT section, not items in a list. Vary the layout, background, and scale of each step dramatically.

better_alternatives: oversized-type-statements — each value is a massive headline (text-7xl+) with 2 lines of supporting text below, stacked vertically with generous spacing
full-bleed-alternating — each value gets its own full-width section alternating light/dark/image backgrounds
editorial-pull-quotes — values as large serif italic quotes with attribution
single-value-per-viewport — one value fills the entire screen, scroll to the next
values_mission.composition_recipe: Values are BELIEFS, not features. Present them with the weight of beliefs — big type, emotional imagery, breathing room. Never as a card grid.

better_alternatives: oversized-fund-names — large outlined or display-weight typography for fund names, stagger-animated on scroll
marquee-ticker-with-frosted-treatment — names scrolling in a frosted-panel strip
editorial-press-layout — large pull quotes from press with publication logo, asymmetric layout, varied card sizes
logo-wall-with-hover-detail — logos at scale with hover revealing investment details
investors_press.composition_recipe: Social proof should feel PRESTIGIOUS, not like a boring directory. Use typography scale and visual weight to convey importance.

better_alternatives: hero-metric-with-subordinates — one number is 3x larger than the others, asymmetric layout
metric-over-photography — numbers overlaid on a relevant full-bleed image with dark overlay
animated-infographic — the numbers are part of a visual diagram, not standalone
before-after-contrast — show the old number crossed out next to the new number
metrics_stats.composition_recipe: One metric should DOMINATE. The others support it. Never give equal visual weight to 4 numbers — create hierarchy by making one dramatically larger.

better_alternatives: horizontal-scroll-stages — each stage is a full panel that scrolls horizontally
animated-flow-diagram — visual arrows/connectors between stages with scroll-triggered progression
split-screen-demo — left shows the UI, right shows the outcome, both animate on scroll
interactive-prototype-mockup — a realistic product UI that steps through the flow
how_it_works.composition_recipe: Show the TRANSFORMATION, not the steps. What does it look like BEFORE and AFTER each stage? The user should feel the progress, not read a numbered list.

better_alternatives: stepped-gradient-with-asymmetric-layout — gradient panels with text on one side, interactive element on the other
split-screen-cta — one half is a bold visual (gradient, image, animation), the other is the action
full-bleed-image-with-glassmorphic-card — real photography with a frosted CTA card floating over it
interactive-roi-calculator-as-cta — the CTA IS a mini-tool that demonstrates value
cta_section.composition_recipe: The CTA should be the CLIMAX of the page, not an afterthought. It should be the most visually striking section. No two CTAs across the site should look the same.

better_alternatives: sticky-scroll-feature-reveal — each feature transforms the visual as you scroll (different image, color shift, element reveal)
split-screen-alternating — feature on left, visual on right, then flip for the next feature
single-feature-per-viewport — one feature fills the screen with bold type + large visual, scroll to next
progressive-disclosure — start with one feature visible, each scroll reveals the next with animation
features.composition_recipe: Features are a STORY, not a grid. Each feature should transform the visual. If you can swap the order and nothing changes visually, you have failed. Each feature deserves its own moment.

better_alternatives: editorial-statement — massive display type IS the section. Let typography + background carry it. No mockup needed.
split-asymmetric — bold headline on 60%, rich visual element on 40%. The visual is NOT a generic dashboard.
full-bleed-visual — real photography or stepped gradient fills the viewport, text overlaid with confidence
interactive-hero — the hero IS a mini-experience (calculator, demo, interactive element)
hero.composition_recipe: The hero sets the emotional tone. It should make the visitor feel something in 2 seconds. A bold statement on a rich background achieves this. A dashboard mockup does not.
